the response rate of a group to a planned conception period is determined by the number of cows assigned and the submission rate, which is influenced by the number of inseminations per cow, and the conception rate, which is affected by repeat breeding, genital disorders and the interval between parturition and the first insemination.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the response rate is the most important factor to be considered when evaluating the effect of a planned conception period on the calving pattern of dairy herds, and that this factor is affected by the submission and conception rates.

the response of a group of cows to a planned conception period depends on the proportion of repeat breeding cows, the proportion of cows with genital disorders, the submission rate of cows and the conception rate.
the response rate of cow groups to a breeding program can be improved by increasing the submission rate and by decreasing the incidence of genital disorders and repeat breeding.
